surfaces.name: Novadeck desktop app (Electron; macOS universal, Windows x64, Linux x86_64 AppImage)
Standalone Novadeck runner (Node service with token-authenticated WebSocket API)

claims.answer: Desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux plus a standalone runner a UI can reach over WebSocket; no mobile app, mobile site, editor extension or end-user CLI for driving agents.

desktop_os.answer: macOS universal dmg, Windows x64 per-user installer and ZIP, Linux x86_64 AppImage; minimum OS versions are not stated.

mobile_apps.answer: No mobile app in the repository; the download page tells phone visitors it is a desktop app.

browser.answer: try.novadeck.dev runs a browser demo and the UI has a browser build that can connect to a runner, but the browser build shows no notifications and there is no hosted web client.

mobile_browser.answer: No mobile web client; the download page redirects phone visitors to a computer.

cli.answer: A novadeck launcher command and the runner CLI (pnpm --filter @novadeck/runner start) exist; there is no CLI for starting or steering agents.

editor_extensions.answer: No editor extension package in apps/ or libraries/.

task_actions.answer: Start agents in terminals, steer by typing, approve permissions and plans from the Inbox, view diffs and pages in the companion pane, and resume sessions after restart.

notifications.answer: Inbox, in-app toasts and OS notifications when an agent asks, finishes or fails.

cross_device_continuity.answer: A standalone runner keeps terminals and accepts several device credentials, so another client can attach; only desktop and browser clients exist.

limitations: No mobile, editor or agent-control CLI client; the browser build is a demo and development target.

claims.answer: Runs the person's own Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode and pi CLIs; each terminal can run a different harness and they can share a team.

harnesses.answer: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity (agy), opencode and pi are connected harnesses with shims and plugins.

model_providers.answer: Novadeck does not choose models; providers are whatever each harness supports.

custom_adapters.answer: Any other CLI runs as a plain terminal; harness adapters are code modules under harnesses/, not a user-configurable adapter.

session_integration.answer: Connected harnesses get hooks and an MCP plugin used for status, messaging and resume.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Agents of different harnesses message each other and can be in one team.

limitations: Model choice stays inside each harness; no generic adapter for other CLIs beyond plain terminals.

claims.answer: Uses the accounts already signed in to each CLI; Novadeck has no account, credits or provider routing, except a hosted onboarding tour that runs on Novadeck's OpenRouter account.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Runs the CLIs with the person's own config and accounts, so Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions apply.

api_accounts.answer: API-key logins configured in each CLI work unchanged.

vendor_credits.answer: Only the onboarding tour runs agents on Novadeck's OpenRouter account; no purchasable credits.

local_models.answer: Local models are possible only through a harness that supports them (for example opencode or pi); Novadeck adds none for agents.

account_switching.answer: No account management; accounts are the CLIs' own.

limitations: No account switching or local-model wiring of its own.
claims.unknownReason: Whether any harness vendor restricts use through a third-party terminal is not stated in Novadeck sources.

claims.answer: Install the app, sign in to at least one agent CLI, tick it in the welcome dialog, then open a folder; git is needed only for worktree and PR features.

first_task_setup.answer: Welcome dialog lists installed agents, installs the plugin, and the agent starts in a terminal.

no_git.answer: Terminals open in any folder; git is used only by worktree and forge features.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Worktrees are created from the local repository; PR lookup needs a remote.

hosted_git.answer: PR status uses GitHub, GitLab or Azure DevOps through the signed-in gh, glab or az CLI.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Guide and welcome dialog name the CLIs to install and the Codex /hooks trust step.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No hosted runtime; the runner doc says there is no public multi-user hosting layer.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Docs describe running the runner on a VPS behind a TLS proxy with systemd or Docker; no guided onboarding.

limitations: No managed cloud setup; remote runner setup is manual.

claims.answer: The runner exposes a token-authenticated WebSocket RPC API, and agents get an MCP tool set inside Novadeck terminals; no public SDK stability promise, webhooks or end-user CLI.

cli.answer: No CLI for creating or steering agent work; only the launcher and runner start command.

api.answer: Runner RPC over WebSocket at /api/rpc with owner token and device credentials.

sdk.answer: @novadeck/runner-client is the in-repo client; not published as a supported SDK.

mcp_server.answer: A Novadeck MCP server (the relay) gives agents send, show, open_agent, lead and related tools.

webhooks.answer: No outgoing webhooks; webhook hits in the source are demo prompts and test fixtures.

operations.answer: Agents can open and close terminals and agents, message, lead teammates and manage worktrees; the runner API covers devices, terminals and preferences.

authentication.answer: Owner token, revocable per-device credentials, and per-terminal tokens for agent relays.

stability.answer: Protocol carries revision numbers with since markers; no external stability guarantee.

limitations: API is the runner protocol used by the UI, versioned by revision but not documented as a public integration surface.

claims.answer: Novadeck installs its own plugin into each harness and otherwise leaves MCP servers, plugins and skills to the harness.

mcp_client.answer: MCP servers are configured in each harness; Novadeck shows MCP elicitation forms in Agent Chat.

plugins.answer: No Novadeck plugin system; the only plugin is Novadeck's own inside each harness.

custom_tools.answer: Custom tools come through the harness; Novadeck adds its own MCP tools.

instructions_import.answer: Harness instruction files apply because the CLIs run unchanged; Novadeck reads none.

authentication.answer: Tool authentication is the harness's; forge tokens come from gh, glab or az.

permission_scope.answer: Claude Code is pre-allowed only Novadeck MCP tools; other permissions stay the harness rules.

integration_owner.answer: Harness vendors own their integrations; Novadeck owns its plugin and relay.

limitations: No Novadeck-level MCP client or extension system.

claims.answer: Harness plans appear for approval in the Inbox and as companion items. File plans can be edited with notes in Novadeck; transcript plans are read-only. Stored pointers and saved files persist, without a task-linked acceptance-criteria model.

plans.answer: Plans from Claude Code and others show in full in the Inbox and companion pane before approval.

editors.answer: The companion pane edits file plans and notes inside the project or harness plan folders; transcript plans are read-only and large plans cannot be edited.

revisions.answer: Source stamps detect concurrent edits and the pane highlights the latest rewrite; there is no durable sequence of immutable plan revisions.

implementation_links.answer: No link from a plan to commits or PRs.

amendment.answer: Send it back returns plan feedback to the agent.

restart_persistence.answer: SQLite keeps plan item pointers and saved edits are in the source file. Reload rereads that file or transcript; deleted source and unsaved pane edits are not recovered.

limitations: The current plan and latest rewrite marks are not an immutable revision history. Unsaved pane edits and deleted source files are not durable.

filesystem.answer: Same user account; worktrees separate checkouts only.

process.answer: Linux terminals run in their own systemd scope and Windows in job objects for lifetime and memory handling, not security.

claims.answer: After a restart terminals reopen in their folders and connected agents resume their sessions; masked transcripts restore plain terminals.

client_disconnect.answer: Runner keeps terminals while clients reconnect.

worker_crash.answer: Crash-loop dialog and restore on next start.

service_restart.answer: SIGTERM saves restore state; terminals come back on next start.

expiry.answer: No session expiry; History keeps closed terminals for 7 days.

transcript_reload.answer: Encrypted masked transcripts reload above a fresh prompt.

process_reconnect.answer: Processes end on restart; agents resume their session rather than reattach.

task_resume.answer: Agents pick up sessions after restart.

context_loss.answer: A program in a plain shell stops on restart; the update card names it.

duplicate_actions.answer: Stable terminal IDs, in-flight start guards and History restore coalescing prevent duplicate terminal restoration; they do not guarantee exactly-once external actions by a resumed harness.

manual_repair.answer: A terminal that could not resume says why.

multi_day_continuity.answer: Projects, sessions and History persist across days.

limitations: Resume depends on the harness plugin. The desktop key is protected by the system keychain; a standalone runner uses a 32-byte key file (created mode 0600), optionally supplied through an encrypted systemd credential or Docker secret. A copy of the complete standalone data folder includes the default key.
Documentation disagrees on History retention: its introduction says 7 days and Closing asks first says 30 days. The pinned pruning code uses 7 days.
contradictions: The reference History introduction says 7 days, while Closing asks first says 30 days. Pinned history.ts prunes after 7 days.

claims.answer: No compute-aware job scheduler. Linux systemd scopes lower background terminal CPU weight and contain many OOM kills; macOS and Windows lower process priority, with platform limitations.

concurrency.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

queues.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

cpu_ram.answer: Linux systemd 253+ scopes set terminal CPUWeight=10 (active terminal 100) and OOMPolicy=continue; absent a usable user bus, they are unavailable. macOS/Windows lower process priority; macOS cannot raise nice back without root.

backpressure.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

host_awareness.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

cancellation.answer: Close ends the terminal and tracked processes. Linux without a user bus and macOS detached processes whose environment cannot be inspected can outlive it; already-running external browser apps also remain.

fairness.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

recovery.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

shared_limits.answer: No scheduler, queues or shared check reuse.

limitations: No job queue, resource admission scheduler or shared test-result cache. Linux scopes require systemd 253+ and a user bus; processes outside a terminal scope are not protected by it. Detached-process cleanup has platform exceptions.

evidence.title: Novadeck README
evidence.finding: Desktop terminal for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode and pi; one Inbox for agent questions; free and open source with no account; runs the CLIs the person already has with their own accounts; macOS, Windows and Linux installers.

evidence.title: Using Novadeck guide
evidence.locator: Connect your agents, Three views, The Inbox, Teams, After a restart
evidence.finding: Welcome dialog installs a small plugin into each ticked agent; Focus, Grid and Canvas views; Inbox for permissions, plans and questions with toasts and system notifications; agents message each other by handle and lead teammates; terminals reopen after restart and closed ones stay in History.

evidence.title: Novadeck reference: Install
evidence.finding: macOS universal dmg/install script, Windows x64 per-user installer and ZIP, Linux x86_64 AppImage; optional AppArmor profile for the Electron sandbox; uninstall keeps projects unless unticked; installed builds auto-update and never restart by themselves.

evidence.title: Novadeck reference: Working in Novadeck
evidence.locator: lines 79-562 (views, Agent Chat, notifications, projects, Inbox, sessions)
evidence.finding: Project switcher shows per-project agent state (working, paused at usage limit, waiting); Inbox lists Unblock, Question, Trouble and Update rows that stay as gray history; desktop system notifications per agent finish or error; projects can be pinned, reordered and removed; sessions group terminals; browser build shows no notifications.

evidence.title: Novadeck reference: History
evidence.locator: History introduction lines 565-567 and conflicting Closing asks first paragraph lines 608-610; implementation cross-check in backend/runner/src/terminals/history.ts lines 38 and 524-536
evidence.finding: The History introduction says closed terminals can be restored for 7 days; the Closing asks first paragraph in the same section still says 30 days. The pinned implementation uses 7 days.

evidence.title: Novadeck reference: Restoring terminals
evidence.locator: lines 626-773 (shell integration, connecting agents, transcripts, permissions)
evidence.finding: After reboot each terminal reopens in its folder and connected agents resume their sessions; connecting installs a Novadeck plugin (hooks and MCP) into each harness; transcripts are masked for secrets and encrypted with an OS keychain key; Claude Code is allowed only Novadeck MCP tools by flag, other permissions stay the harness own.

evidence.title: Agent messaging: Agent interface
evidence.finding: Inside Novadeck terminals agents get MCP tools send, show, look, open_terminal, open_agent, close_terminal, lead and release, plus worktree tools when enabled; send answers queued, held or refused and never claims delivery.

evidence.title: Agent messaging: Herd, Solo and Swarm
evidence.finding: Preference picks how far agents act on each other: Herd (default) lets agents settle overlaps directly; Solo and Swarm sit behind an experimental switch; Swarm lets agents open, lead and close teammates without asking.

evidence.title: Agent messaging: The shipping gate
evidence.finding: Experimental, off by default: gates gh pr create, gh pr merge and pushes or ref moves outside the agent own worktree branch behind an Inbox permit; only exact commands a live permit covers are allowed.

evidence.title: Agent workspace: Worktrees
evidence.finding: Experimental agent worktrees (Preferences, Experimental, off by default): open_worktree, take_worktree, close_worktree, give_worktree create and track git worktrees under ~/.novadeck/worktrees with owner terminal, branch and base recorded; the Worktrees panel measures each against its home branch.

evidence.title: runner worktrees repo.ts

evidence.title: runner shipping reader.ts
evidence.locator: header comment and permit keys, lines 1-95
evidence.finding: Shipping targets are gh pr create, gh pr merge (with separate --auto and --admin targets) and pushes or ref moves; permits are keyed by repository and branch or PR number.

evidence.title: @novadeck/forges README

evidence.title: Backend API: Running a standalone runner

evidence.title: Novadeck MCP tools (shell/mcp.ts)
evidence.locator: header comment lines 14-17; model and effort properties lines 539-565
evidence.finding: open_agent opens a terminal running another connected harness, on a model and effort when asked, with a brief as its task; the runner lists each harness's models and efforts.

evidence.title: Novadeck SubscriptionUsage footer component
evidence.locator: WindowRow and UsageDetail, lines 30-60; mounted in frontend/ui/src/app/FooterSection.tsx line 368
evidence.finding: The footer shows each connected agent subscription with its usage windows as bars, the used share and when each window resets, as the agent reports them.

evidence.title: Novadeck agentStats (frontend/core/src/agents/stats.ts)
evidence.locator: AgentStats type and agentStats, lines 14-45; rendered by frontend/ui/src/app/WorkspaceTerminal.tsx line 230
evidence.finding: Each agent terminal window shows the model, effort and how full its context is, as a share or as tokens held; these are live readings, not totals or statistics.

evidence.title: Novadeck auto-update design
evidence.finding: Setting NOVADECK_UPDATES=off turns update checks off for a launch; the Preferences Updates section has only the Experimental channel switch, no update-check switch.

evidence.title: Novadeck runner source search for retries, run limits and traces
evidence.locator: rg -ni 'retr(y|ies)|timeout|max_?turns|trace|statistic|usage.{0,20}export' across backend/runner/src, harnesses and frontend, with production hits inspected separately from test/spec fixtures
evidence.finding: No agent run-time or turn cap, usage export or aggregate statistics module was found in the scoped implementation. Retry paths handle delivery/files/engine operations, not rerunning failed agent turns. Production doorbell tracing exists in messaging/doorbell-log.ts and is wired by apps/desktop/src/runner/index.ts; it is not only test code.

evidence.title: Novadeck History pruning
evidence.finding: History uses a seven-day retention interval and deletes closed-terminal rows older than that cutoff. The reference introduction agrees; its Closing asks first paragraph still says 30 days.

evidence.title: Novadeck plan editor
evidence.finding: The companion plan pane edits file plans and notes and highlights the latest rewrite. Transcript plans are read-only; unsaved changes can be lost when the pane closes. Revision stamps support conflict handling, not an immutable plan history.

evidence.title: Novadeck plan save
evidence.finding: File plans are reread from disk. Save compares the source stamp, limits editing to regular plan files inside project or harness plan folders, caps at 256 KiB, and renames a temporary file over the original. Transcript plans remain read-only.

evidence.title: Novadeck plan store
evidence.locator: items/saveItem lines 3003-3080; companions/records.ts ItemRecord; companions/items.ts planObserved/observe
evidence.finding: SQLite companion_items stores a plan pointer with stable item id, path, agent/session and format. It is not a copy or acceptance-criteria/task model. Surviving pointers reread file or transcript content; loss of source makes the item unavailable.

evidence.title: Novadeck doorbell traces
evidence.locator: createDoorbellLog lines 49-135; logDoorbell lines 181-197; wired in apps/desktop/src/runner/index.ts line 53
evidence.finding: Production tracing keeps the latest 100 decision lines per terminal in memory, logs them on ring failure or after messages wait five minutes, and emits debug trace lines. Verbose mode also logs selected screen rows. This is a diagnostic log, not an end-to-end task trace viewer.

evidence.title: Novadeck open budgets
evidence.locator: New terminals lines 880-900; docs/agent-messaging.md Agent interface; backend/runner/src/messaging/send-rates.ts
evidence.finding: The runner limits opening to five terminals or fifteen led teammates per minute from a shared initiating chain budget, and twenty per minute runner-wide. Messaging has separate sender/pair/runner limits and holds idle loops; these are not token, dollar or agent-run deadlines.

evidence.title: Novadeck restore deduplication
evidence.finding: freshShell rejects duplicate starts while entry.starting, uses stable terminal IDs, and does not resume into a live conflicting shell. History restore coalesces identical in-flight IDs, reuses a matching restored terminal, and refuses a second competing restore of the same row. These guards do not provide exactly-once external side effects for harness work.

evidence.title: Novadeck desktop update checks at commit 8dd943a
evidence.locator: apps/desktop/src/main/updates/updater.ts lines 26-30 (first check 10 s after launch, then hourly, each counted on novadeck.dev), 44-54 (CheckFacts: version and installed/portable build so the website can count active copies), 123-130 (checkHeaders), 193-203 (updaterKind; looksForUpdates requires a packaged nonzero version and NOVADECK_UPDATES not off); apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts line 187 (crashReporter uploadToServer false)
evidence.finding: Packaged builds with a real version check novadeck.dev for updates 10 seconds after launch and then hourly, adding the check reason, version and installed or portable build so the website can count active copies. A launch with NOVADECK_UPDATES=off makes no checks. Native crash dumps are kept locally and never uploaded.

evidence.title: Novadeck auto-update design: what a check sends and how the website counts it
evidence.finding: Update checks read novadeck.dev, which counts each request to know how many copies are open and launched, then answers with the release file from GitHub. A check adds only its reason, version and build, and the per-install staging ID is patched out; the requested file name still reveals the system. Windows, macOS and Linux AppImage builds check; local, pull request and development builds do not.

evidence.title: Novadeck privacy (last changed 25 November 2026)
evidence.locator: What the app sends; feedback card; uninstall goodbye page; nightly AI sorting; onboarding tour; Who else sees your requests; Why, and who to ask
evidence.finding: The app sends no code, terminals, chats or logs except during the onboarding tour. Update checks send reason, version and build with no ID; the site keeps only the country and counts copies open each hour by channel and system and launches each day by version, build and country. Feedback notes are sent only on Send; the uninstaller opens a goodbye page whose answers are kept only when clicked. Both are anonymous, kept 12 months and cannot be deleted on request. Each night an AI model sorts the last month of notes into themes through OpenRouter, only to providers that do not train; themes are kept at most two months. Tour ticket rows are deleted after 90 days. Cloudflare, GitHub, OpenRouter, Microsoft Azure and Hugging Face are named; requests may be handled outside the EU.
